fields.meta_description: Take a free spirit animal quiz that matches your answers to an animal, then build one for a sanctuary, library, camp, or museum. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Spirit Animal Quiz Where Every Animal Has Its Own Page
fields.hero_description: Build a spirit animal quiz with a result page for each animal, and try the 8-question version below first.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Spirit Animal Quiz
fields.features_subheading: A spirit animal quiz matches each answer to an animal. Emergent builds the questions, a page per animal, and the table behind them.
fields.feature_1:
Options that each point to one animal

Name the animals first and say what kind of visitor each one fits. Emergent writes the questions with every option tied to one animal, and it changes any wording you ask it to.
fields.feature_2:
A page for every animal

Each result opens its own page with the animal's photo, two lines on the habits the answers leaned toward, and a link you pick, such as a trail map or an adoption page.
fields.feature_3:
Results saved beside the answers

Every finished quiz is a row in a database you own: the animal, each option picked, the date, and an email if the visitor left one. Sort by animal to see which result comes up.
fields.feature_4:
Lists for the people who follow up

Send a Slack message or an email when a result needs a person, such as a camp counselor who reads the cabin list the night before arrival. Pick the time it goes out.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen on a tablet

Visitors answer one question per screen, which suits a phone or a lobby tablet. Emergent puts no cap on responses, and a busy Saturday at a museum records every play.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, with the code in GitHub

Publish the quiz on your own domain, included in Emergent and charged in credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and host it wherever you choose.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Places That Run a Spirit Animal Quiz
fields.tab_content_1:
Every otter result opens with an adoption link

Teodora Vance answers the last question of Harrow Ridge Wildlife Sanctuary's spirit animal quiz and gets River Otter. The result screen introduces Pip, one of the sanctuary's 2 otters, and links to the otter adoption page. Her result and email land in the supporters table, tagged River Otter.
fields.tab_content_2:
Three owl books for Rafi to borrow

Summer reading sign-up at the Kessler Branch of Alder Falls Public Library ends with a spirit animal quiz. Rafi, age 9, gets Great Horned Owl. His result card lists 3 owl books on the Kessler shelf, pulled from the library catalog through its API. The sign-up saves his first name, age, branch, and animal.
fields.tab_content_3:
Cabin 4's animals, sent to Bryn before arrival

Families get Camp Wendmoor's spirit animal quiz with the packing list for the July 6 session. At 6 p.m. on July 5, counselor Bryn Castellano gets an email listing the 8 campers in Cabin 4 and each camper's animal. She opens the first-night circle by asking the 2 wolves to go first.
fields.tab_content_4:
410 wolf results in March, and a new Saturday talk

A tablet by the mammal hall entrance at Brightwater Natural History Museum runs the quiz one question per screen. In March it logged 1,260 plays: Gray Wolf 410, Great Horned Owl 330, River Otter 300, and Red-tailed Hawk 220. The education team read the dashboard and added a Saturday wolf talk.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Spirit Animal Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a spirit animal quiz where every animal can come up and each result leads somewhere, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the animals before the questions
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write each result as a preference
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Map one option to each animal
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose 4 animals before writing a single question, and give each one a two-line description of the habits it stands for. Four results suit an 8-question quiz, and every option you write later needs one of these animals to point to.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Describe what the answers lean toward, such as quiet evenings or noisy group trips, instead of telling the reader who they are. Keep each description short enough to read on a phone, and give every animal the same warm tone.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask what people do on an ordinary day: the seat they pick on a bus, or their plan for a rainy Sunday. Read each set of options aloud and rewrite any option that sounds nicer than the other three.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Point one option in every question to each animal, which gives each result 8 chances. Pick the tie rule before launch, such as the animal listed first, then play the quiz once as each animal to confirm all 4 can win.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Keep it to 8 questions with 4 options each. A visitor at a lobby tablet or on a phone can finish in one sitting, and every extra question adds one more screen between the visitor and the result.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before launch, ask five people outside the project to play it. Note which animal each one gets and whether the description fits the answers they gave. If one animal never comes up, reword the options that point to it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Decide what each result links to
fields.howto_step_7_des: Give every result a next step: an adoption page, a book list, a trail map, or news about that animal. Keep the email field optional and ask for it after the result. Nobody should have to sign up to see their animal.

faq_plan.q: What is a spirit animal quiz?
faq_plan.a: A spirit animal quiz is a short quiz that matches your answers to one animal and describes what your choices lean toward. Each option points to an animal, and the animal with the most picks is your result. The term borrows from spirit animals, which UW-Madison's housing guide describes as spiritual guides that take the form of animals often viewed as sacred in tribal cultures.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a spirit animal quiz?
faq_plan.a: Name the animals, the number of questions, and where each result should lead, and Emergent's AI survey builder writes the quiz, a page for each animal, and the table that stores every result. Change any question with a follow-up prompt, then publish the link.

faq_plan.q: Can I make a free spirit animal quiz for my website?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing. Describe your animals and questions in one prompt and publish the quiz. Link to it from any page of your site. Each finished quiz is saved to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do I make an online spirit animal quiz result feel accurate?
faq_plan.a: Build each result from the options that lead to it. If the otter's options are swimming, a crowded table, and a game night, the otter result should name those habits back to the reader. A style quiz works the same way, with clothes and colors in place of animals.

faq_plan.q: What should the result screen of a what's my spirit animal quiz show?
faq_plan.a: Show the animal's name and a photo first, then two lines on what the answers leaned toward. Under that, add one next step, like the trail where that animal lives or a book list, and a share link that opens the same result page for a friend.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep one animal from winning most of the time in my spirit animal quiz?
faq_plan.a: Count the results after the first 100 plays. With 4 animals, each should land near 25. If one takes 40 or more, move one of its options to the animal with the fewest results. On Emergent, a follow-up prompt changes the mapping, and the next visitor plays the new version.

faq_plan.q: Can a spirit animal quiz teach kids facts about animals?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the result pages carry the facts and you check each one against a zoo or wildlife group's own page. The quiz itself sorts preferences and has no right answers. For questions with one correct option and a score, use the format of a vocabulary quiz instead, with score bands for the result.

faq_plan.q: Is it respectful to call my quiz a spirit animal quiz?
faq_plan.a: Not to every reader: some people object to the term. UW-Madison's inclusive language guide says non-native people appropriate the term to relate themselves to an animal. A title such as 'What is your animal match?' keeps the spirit animal quiz format without the term, and the quiz on this page uses one.

faq_plan.q: Can I run my animal spirit quiz on a tablet at an event?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask for one question per screen and a restart button on the result page, which sends the next visitor back to question 1. There is no cap on responses in an Emergent app, and every play at a busy event is saved with its animal and the time it finished.

faq_plan.q: Where should I share my spirit animal quiz?
faq_plan.a: Share it where your visitors already look: the newsletter, a social post, a QR code on a sign by an exhibit, or the homepage. For a product sign-up, a 4-question version can sit above the form on a free trial landing page. Track which link brought each play in the results table.

quiz.title: What Is Your Animal Match?
quiz.intro: Eight questions about how you spend your time. Each answer points to one of 4 animals, and your result names the animal your choices lean toward.

questions.text: It's a free Saturday. How does it start?

options.text: A slow breakfast and a book before anyone else is up
A swim or a paddle with friends
A long hike with the same group as always
A drive somewhere new with no fixed plan

questions.text: Which seat do you pick on a long bus ride?

options.text: The middle, where the card game is
Front row, watching the road ahead
A window seat near the back, headphones on
Next to your best friend, saving seats for the rest

questions.text: A group project lands on your desk. Which part do you take?

options.text: Making sure no one falls behind
The research nobody else wants to read
Setting the plan and the deadline
Keeping everyone laughing through the late nights

questions.text: Pick a place to spend an afternoon.

options.text: A cliff-top lookout over the valley
A lake with a rope swing
A quiet corner of the library
A campfire with old friends

questions.text: How do you handle a big decision?

options.text: Read everything first and sleep on it
Ask the people closest to you
Talk it over with whoever is around
Decide fast and adjust later
A loud game night that runs late
Family dinner at a long table
A sunset from the highest point in town
Stargazing with a thermos of cocoa

questions.text: What do friends count on you to bring to a party?

options.text: The rides, since you planned who sits where
The playlist, picked an hour before
The trivia questions
The pool games and the snacks

questions.text: Pick a souvenir from a trip.

options.text: A postcard from the farthest stop
An old map from a used bookstore
Matching bracelets for the whole group
A photo of everyone soaked after a boat ride

results.title: Great Horned Owl
results.description: Your answers lean toward quiet mornings, a good book, and time to think before you choose. You like knowing the details first, and your best afternoons happen in a corner where nobody interrupts.

results.title: River Otter
results.description: Your answers lean toward water, games, and a crowded table. You like plans that leave room for fun, and a long day goes better with a group to share it.

results.title: Gray Wolf
results.description: Your answers lean toward your own people: the same hiking group, a long family dinner, and saved seats on the bus. You like making sure nobody gets left behind.

results.title: Red-tailed Hawk
results.description: Your answers lean toward wide views and quick decisions. You like setting the plan, heading somewhere new, and watching the road from the front row.

plan.angle: The top 10 is consumer spirit animal quizzes (an apparel shop, BuzzFeed, a symbolism site, WCS, WWF, a career-test site, Reddit, teen magazines). None shows how to build one. This page lets a visitor play a full animal-matching quiz, then shows four organizations running their own: a wildlife sanctuary linking each result to that animal's adoption page, a public library handing out a book list per animal at summer reading sign-up, a summer camp emailing counselors their cabin's results, and a museum counting tablet plays per animal. The FAQ covers naming the quiz with care, writing results, balancing them, and collecting emails, with every answer saved to a database the owner keeps.
